newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled little changed on Monday after failing to break through Friday's close in a subdued session, hampered by the lack of price direction from the U.S. bond market which was closed for a holiday.

The March bond contract touched its low for the day in the first half of trading at 132.12, above a supportive gap between 131.96-132.10, and briefly tested Friday's close of 132.44 late during the day.
However volume was low with just 50,459 contracts changing hands and traders said although the market remained relatively bullish it was in a delicate phase, just below record highs.

Monday's trading was seen mainly as a day of consolidation after the contract set a record high at 132.50 on Friday and some traders said with profit taking out of the way there was a chance it could reach new ground on Tuesday.

There was little concern about German M3 money supply due later this week and few expected any change in interest rates after the Bundesbank's regular policy council meeting on Thursday. Traders said the German Ifo business survey would probably be the most significant report this week.
PIBOR contracts settled slightly lower after an equally subdued session.
